Qcar - Block 1 (JMF, fault detection) De.Purpose: Implement a fault detection system for the Qcar project using JMF (Jump Markov Filter). The system will monitor vehicle parameters and identify potential faults in real-time.

current_progress: Restored topic advertising and confirmed /sup_jmf/odom, /sup_jmf/mode_prob, /sup_jmf/current_mode are visible on the ROS bus.
Removed all position‐based updates (pose_lidar & noisy_odom) so the filter state (vx, vy, r, biases) matches only IMU+velocity.
Verified JMF::init() correctly loads the π matrix via Eigen::Map<RowMajor> and prints it on startup.
Implemented Likelihood flooring (raw_like = max(norm_const*exp(-0.5·maha), 1e-12)) to prevent exact zero underflow.
Added node‐level hysteresis: declared_mode only switches if a new mode’s probability exceeds 80% for 3 consecutive cycles, suppressing transient dips.
Confirmed Mahalanobis distances for IMU and velocity updates now reside in a realistic range (0–20) most of the time, and raw likelihoods remain nonzero.
Integrated fusedState() and fusedCovariance() publishing alongside TF from 'odom' to 'base_link' at 50 Hz without crashes.
JMF core is fully functional inside ROS; predict/update cycles perform as expected, mixing IMM priors and computing five per‐mode EKF updates each IMU tick.
missing_components: Tune R_imu and R_vel values (or implement log‐likelihood) so that underflow floors never trigger a uniform 0.2 reset after a single outlier.
Implement multi‐cycle fallback logic inside JumpMarkovFilter::update() to skip uniform resetting unless likelihoods remain near floor for N cycles.
Expose and publish explicit fault_detected, fault_type, and fault_severity flags based on mode_prob and hysteresis state.
Write unit tests (Google Test) for JMF: exercising Q, R tuning, likelihood flooring, and multi‐cycle fallback behavior.
Add diagnostic_updater hooks to stream innovation norms, mahalanobis distances, and raw likelihood vectors for offline tuning.
